protocol.name: cutefish_shell_v1

description.summary: private shell surface roles for cutefish-shell

protocol.description:
This protocol lets the trusted Cutefish shell process describe what its surfaces are for: a desktop background, a panel, a dock, the launcher, a notification banner, the on-screen display or the screen capture interface.
It is an *extension* of an ordinary wl_surface, not a replacement for xdg-shell. The shell keeps creating xdg_toplevel objects through xdg_wm_base exactly like any other Wayland client; this protocol only adds the role, the stacking behaviour, the global position, the focus policy and the work-area reservation that plain xdg-shell cannot express.
The compositor only advertises this global to the one trusted shell client it was handed by the session. Ordinary applications never see it.
Warning! Not a standard protocol. Backward-incompatible changes are made by bumping the interface version.

description.summary: private shell interface

entry.name: role
entry.summary: the wl_surface already has a cutefish_shell_surface_v1

request.name: destroy

description.summary: release the shell interface

request.description: Destroying the factory does not destroy the shell surfaces it created.

request.name: get_shell_surface

description.summary: extend a wl_surface with shell metadata

request.description:
Creates a cutefish_shell_surface_v1 for the given wl_surface.
The wl_surface must belong to the same client and the same connection. Giving a surface two shell surfaces raises the role error.
The metadata carried by the new object should be set before the first buffer is committed on the surface, so the compositor never has to place the surface as an ordinary window first.

request.name: get_drag

description.summary: follow a drag this client starts

request.description: Creates a cutefish_shell_drag_v1 that follows the drag-and-drop operation this client has in progress, or else the next one it starts with wl_data_device.start_drag. Drags started by other clients are never followed.

interface.name: cutefish_shell_surface_v1

description.summary: shell metadata attached to a wl_surface

interface.description: Describes what the compositor should make of a shell surface. All state here takes effect immediately rather than on the next wl_surface.commit: the shell sets it once when the surface is created and the compositor applies it to the window the surface's xdg role produces.

enum.name: role

description.summary: what the surface is

enum.description:
The role decides which stacking layer the window lives in and how the window manager places it. Roles other than desktop are always kept in their own layer: activation can never move a window between layers.
A capture surface and its popups are shown on screen but never painted into an image or a video the compositor captures, so the interface that takes a screenshot is never part of it.
A capture surface never becomes the active window: activating it only takes the keyboard, and the window that was active stays active.
An osd surface never takes the keyboard, whatever its focus policy, and it stays above the notification banners.
A sheet surface is window-modal for the window given by set_parent: it is stacked right above that window, kept centred on it as the window moves or either of them resizes, shown and hidden with it and kept on its desk. Its position is the compositor's.

entry.name: panel
entry.summary: a panel such as the status bar

entry.name: capture
entry.summary: the screen capture interface, above everything else

entry.name: osd
entry.summary: the on-screen display of a volume or brightness change

entry.name: sheet
entry.summary: a dialog hanging from an application window, see set_parent

enum.name: panel_behavior

description.summary: how a panel or dock relates to ordinary windows

enum.description: Only meaningful for the panel and dock roles.

entry.name: windows_can_cover
entry.summary: ordinary windows and the launcher may be stacked over it

entry.name: normal
entry.summary: the window can take keyboard focus

entry.name: no_focus
entry.summary: the window receives pointer input but never keyboard focus

description.summary: which screen edge an exclusive zone is measured from

request.name: destroy

description.summary: drop the shell metadata

request.description: The surface goes back to being an ordinary window, and any exclusive zone it reserved is released.

request.name: set_role

description.summary: set the surface role

request.description: Must be sent before the surface is first mapped. Changing the role of a mapped surface is allowed but the compositor may only apply it the next time the surface is mapped.

request.name: set_position

description.summary: place the surface in global coordinates

request.description: The position of the surface's top left corner in the compositor's global coordinate space. A shell surface is never subject to the window manager's ordinary placement policy: this position is authoritative.

request.name: set_exclusive_zone

description.summary: reserve work area along a screen edge

request.description:
Asks the compositor to keep a strip of `thickness` logical pixels along `edge` clear of maximized and normally placed windows.
Reservations from every shell surface compose: a status bar at the top and a dock at the bottom shrink the work area from both ends. A thickness of zero is the same as clear_exclusive_zone.

description.summary: release this surface's work-area reservation

request.name: activate

description.summary: give this surface the keyboard focus

request.description:
The trusted way for the launcher to take focus. No serial is required: the shell is trusted, and its own activations do not come from an input event it can point at.
Ignored while the surface has no window, or while its focus policy is no_focus.

request.name: set_output

description.summary: associate this surface with a logical output

request.description: Selects the logical output by its stable wl_output name. Positions stay in global coordinates. Exclusive zones apply only to this output.

request.name: set_parent

description.summary: the application window a sheet belongs to

request.description: The identifier cutefish_window_management_v1.window announced the window with. Only meaningful for the sheet role, and best sent before the first commit; a mapped sheet moves to its new parent. A window that is gone, or zero, leaves the sheet on its own, placed like any other shell surface.

interface.name: cutefish_shell_drag_v1

description.summary: where a drag of the shell's goes and how it ends

interface.description:
Reports the pointer of one drag in global coordinates, wherever it is and whatever surface is under it, and tells a drop from a cancel. After dropped or cancelled only returned may follow, and the object should then be destroyed.
Where the shell's drag may go is the shell's to say: while the drag is over nothing that takes the drop, the pointer keeps its default shape rather than showing that it cannot drop there.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: stop following the drag

request.description: Also lets go of an icon that is sliding back or waits where it arrived; see returned.

request.name: set_icon_opacity

description.summary: how opaque the drag icon is drawn

request.description: From 0 to 1. It holds for the rest of the drag the object follows, and may be sent before that drag starts.

request.name: set_returns_home

description.summary: whether an untaken drag's icon goes back

request.description: Nonzero makes the drag icon slide back to where it was when the drag started if the drag ends with nothing taking the data: cancelled, or let go over nothing that accepts it. The returned event tells when it is back. Zero, the initial value, lets the icon go where the drag ends. What counts is the value when the drag ends; it may be sent before the drag starts.

request.name: set_home

description.summary: where a returning drag goes back to

request.description: The point, in global logical coordinates, the drag's pointer position goes back to when its icon returns; the icon keeps its offset from it. Until this is sent, it is where the drag started.

event.name: motion

description.summary: the drag moved

event.description: Sent when the drag starts and whenever its pointer moves, in global logical coordinates.

event.name: dropped

description.summary: the drag was let go

event.description: Sent where the drag was let go, whether or not a target takes the data, and before any wl_data_source event about the drop.

event.name: cancelled

description.summary: the drag ended without a drop

event.description: Escape, or the drag's source or origin surface went away.

event.name: returned

description.summary: the icon is back where the drag started

event.description:
Sent after dropped or cancelled when the drag ended with nothing taking the data while set_returns_home was nonzero, once the icon has slid back; at once when the drag had no icon to slide.
The icon then stays where it arrived until this object is destroyed, so the client can destroy it once a frame of its own shows the icon there, and no frame shows both or neither.
